turns.match: explain how a heat pump works, step by step
turns.script:
look blueprint
scene layout=figure canvas=wide lines=4
color hot=#ff8a5c cold=#7cc8ff
rect house 4,10 70x70 stroke=ink thick=0.6
say x1 label at=39,14 | inside
say x2 label at=118,14 | outside
rect coil_in 14,30 14x34 fill=hot
rect coil_out 130,30 14x34 fill=cold
rect comp 64,64 28x14 r=2 fill=accent
rect valve 72,22 12x10 fill=dim
line hotpipe 28,36 64,71 stroke=hot thick=1.5
line hotpipe2 28,58 72,27 stroke=cold thick=1
line cp 92,71 130,58 stroke=hot thick=1.5
line vp 84,27 130,36 stroke=cold thick=1
say x3 callout near=coil_out | evaporator
say x4 callout near=comp | compressor
say x5 callout near=coil_in | condenser
say x6 callout near=valve | expansion valve
say x7 | 1. Cold refrigerant in the outdoor coil soaks up heat from the air, even at freezing temperatures, and boils into a gas.
wait 1
say x8 | 2. The compressor squeezes that gas, making it much hotter.
hit comp pulse
say x9 | 3. The hot gas releases its heat into your home through the indoor coil and condenses back into a liquid.
hit coil_in pulse
say x10 | 4. The expansion valve drops its pressure, so it turns very cold, and it flows back outside to start again.
hit valve pulse
wait 1
say x11 strong | It *moves* heat, giving 3 to 4 times the energy it uses.
say x12 choice | How does it cool in summer?
say x13 choice | Why does it struggle in deep cold?
line hotpipe 28,58 64,71 stroke=hot thick=1.5
line hotpipe2 28,36 72,27 stroke=cold thick=1

hit coil_out pulse
correct x10 | Winter is this same loop. The outdoor coil runs colder than the frosty air, so heat still flows into it.
correct x11 | The colder it gets, the harder it works: about 3 times the energy it uses at 7C, closer to 2 times at -15C.
drop x12
drop x13
say x14 aside | Frost builds up on the outdoor coil, so every so often the heat pump briefly runs in reverse to melt it. In very hard cold, a backup heater helps out.
say x15 choice | Why does it struggle in deep cold?
say x16 choice | How does it cool in summer?
